vars.team_intro: For significant features or changes that are more than a few lines of code, run a team of Codex subagents with a structured multi-agent approach. You are the lead: spawn each role with `spawn_agent` using its agent type, leave `fork_context` off so every role starts with only the prompt you give it, and use `wait_agent` to finish a step before starting the next.
vars.worktree_section: **All agents share one workspace dir.** Before spawning any agent, run `team-guard workspace new <feature>`, then `team-guard workspace attach <repo-path>` from the workspace dir for each repo the feature touches. Each attached worktree is on the same branch name in its repo. Start Codex from the workspace dir so every subagent inherits it as its working directory; each agent edits code inside `repos/<repo>/`, and the workflow artifacts stay in the workspace dir.
vars.role_files: Role definitions are in `~/.codex/agents/` (`<role>.toml`). A project can override one with its own in `.codex/agents/`.
vars.design_review: Run `crit design.md` from the workspace so the human can comment (Crit renders the diagrams), or post the doc in chat. The architect revises from comments. The human approves in Crit, or replies `approve design` in chat.
vars.human_gate: Show the human the draft and the full diff, test changes included. Nothing is pushed without approval.
vars.ship: After approval run `team-guard sign --base origin/<base branch>` in the workspace (with `TEAM_SANDBOX=1` it skips signing and the commits stay unsigned: say so in the PR draft; only the workspace image sets it, never set it yourself), push, and open the PR.
vars.review_stop: the code review before any push
vars.first_push: The first push needs the human's approval. After that, sign a fix
vars.security_stop: A security fix, or a vulnerability in existing code that the security review finds, stops the work before any push: the details stay in the workspace and the human decides.
